lyrics:
[Intro: ticking piano figure, vinyl hiss, distant scratches]

[Verse 1: male rap, steady, drums and bass enter]
I built it out of weekends, out of favours, out of nerve
Drew the plans on a napkin, learned the rest on the curve
Put my name on the door and my savings in the floor
Told my mother it was working when I couldn't tell her more
Every year a little louder, every year a little thin
Kept on pouring in the hours where the cracks were getting in
And I held it, and I held it, till my hands forgot the rest
Then I watched it fold on a Tuesday, no alarm and no protest

[Chorus: raspy tenor sings, wall of guitars]
I gave it all I had
And I watched it fall
And for the longest time
I thought that that was all
But I'd do it the same
I'd lose it again
It turns out the trying
Is the part that I keep

[Verse 2: male rap, more personal, piano answers]
Same thing with the two of us, I'll say it while I can
I learned your coffee order, I learned your mother's plans
Showed up for the hard days, showed up for the worse
Read the books and did the work and said the sorry first
Still, you can do it right and watch it walk away
There isn't any scoreboard, there isn't any pay
I used to think that meant the whole thing was a lie
Now I think it means I'm someone who will try

[Chorus: raspy tenor sings, wall of guitars]
I gave it all I had
And I watched it fall
And for the longest time
I thought that that was all
But I'd do it the same
I'd lose it again
It turns out the trying
Is the part that I keep

[Bridge: quiet piano, then building to screamed lines]
Nobody keeps the trophy
Nobody keeps the room
You only keep the reaching
So reach
So reach

[Final Chorus: both voices, heaviest, rap ad-libs between lines]
I gave it all I had
And I watched it fall
And for the longest time
I thought that that was all
But I'd do it the same
I'd lose it again
It turns out the trying
Is the part that I keep

[Outro: piano figure alone, slowing, last note left hanging]
The part that I keep
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 105 BPM, 4/4, E-flat minor. Measured and heavy, with a steady tick underneath. Sad, then defiant.

VOICE: Two men. A rapper with a clear, even, unhurried delivery who sounds like he is reading out evidence. A singer with a raspy tenor who starts the chorus melodically and pushes into a rough, powerful shout, and screams two lines in the bridge. They overlap in the last chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: A simple, repeating piano figure in a high register, the song's signature. Thick, down-tuned distorted guitars that enter only for the choruses. Deep bass. A tight hip-hop-influenced drum kit with a dry snare. Turntable scratches and vinyl hiss. A soft string pad. A filtered electronic beat under the verses.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the piano figure alone with hiss and scratches. 0:18 Verse 1, drums and bass. 0:55 Chorus 1, the guitars arrive. 1:22 Verse 2. 1:59 Chorus 2. 2:26 Bridge, piano alone for two lines, then a build to two screamed words. 2:46 Final chorus, both voices. 3:13 Outro, everything stops except the piano, which slows and leaves its last note hanging at 3:35.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Turn-of-the-century nu-metal with pop precision: verses dry and narrow, choruses enormous and wide, every transition sharp.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The piano figure alone at the start. Three notes in, anyone who was a teenager in 2001 knows what kind of song it is.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original says effort came to nothing. This is the same man twenty-five years on, who has lost more and has changed his mind about what counts.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Inventory, loss, a second look, resolve.
